The list of his achievements — ending the influence of Communism in America's backyard, ensuring the dismantling of "evil empires", regularly condemning his adversaries as "evil" without specifying what he meant by "evil", destroying Saddam Hussein in three glorious days in 1991, becoming arguably the most effective person ever elected to public office in America — is impressive. He dumbed down American arts, culture and education — first through nostalgia-based boy bands and teen idols in films and shows, then through Romans-Gladiators-Romans films which insisted on schoolchildren taking up more Roman than American history. He even introduced what looked like hallucinogens in the USA through the now-infamous jelly beans (his words). His necessarily diminished view of the White House (before him, every president described the Oval Office as "my home": after him, George W Bush described it as reminiscent of "Fortress Lincoln") meant that post-administration was always going to be a disaster.

Supported by Conservative MP for Bournemouth West Conor Burns, of the Y3M Parliamentary Group, the court case was the result of three Labour MPs' concern over the inclusion of the word "urban" and the 2017 roll-out of local plans due to be published by the Conservatives for councils in Wales and Scotland.
